subject: Post-demo blueprint: SDK + auth + model-routing for CatalystPay
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Lee Harper <lee.harper@catalystpay.com>, Amira Khan <amira.khan@catalystpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-09T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo blueprint: SDK + auth + model-routing for CatalystPay

Hi Lee / Amira — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and a pragmatic blueprint so your eng team can start implementation in parallel to the commercial next steps. TL;DR: SDK init + auth, routing policy, and a lightweight fallback chain we recommend to keep latency predictable while controlling spend.

What we covered (notes for your engineers):
- SDK setup: use our Node + Python SDKs; we recommend Server-side SDK (no browser tokens) with short-lived session tokens. Example snippet in attached PDF.
- Auth: mTLS for production (required for private VPC), OAuth2 + token exchange OK for hosted. If you want SSO + SCIM, we can include that in the SOW.
- Routing & model selection: primary route -> high-accuracy LLM (redwood-llm-xxl) for transactions and policy-sensitive output; cost-sensitive route -> quantized medium model for high-volume text or simple classification.
- Fallback chain: 1) primary model (aa) -> 2) quantized medium model (bb) -> 3) cached-response or reranker-only path for embeddings/rerank (cc). We propose QoS rules: max latency threshold 350ms for primary, 700ms for fallback.
- Structured output & tools: Use our JSON schema enforcement and tool-calling facility for payment routing decisions; attach example schema in PDF.
- Embeddings/rerank: we suggest an embeddings index for 30-day recency and a reranker to reduce token spend when candidate set > 5.

Next concrete steps (owner):
- CatalystPay: share the list of endpoints and internal SRE contact for cert provisioning (action: Lee) — target by EOD Friday.
- Redwood: provide a trimmed SDK starter repo and auth diagrams (action: Monica) — sending attachments with this email.
- Technical sync: 30m with your eng-ops to walk through mTLS and model fallback config (action: Ben/Karthik). Proposed slots: Mon/Tue next week.

Risks & asks:
- If your production SRE cannot provision mTLS certs quickly, we can keep a hosted OAuth path but require extra guards around PII (we'll add masking).
- If you need sub-150ms tail latency for authorization calls we should discuss dedicated capacity.

Attachments: catalystpay_integration_blueprint_v1.pdf (blueprint, code snippets), catalystpay_sdk_auth_diagram.png (auth flow).

Thanks — I’ll schedule the technical sync once Lee confirms the SRE contact.

— Monica Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Lee Harper <lee.harper@catalystpay.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Amira Khan <amira.khan@catalystpay.com>, eng-ops@catalystpay.com
Date: 2028-11-09T18:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo blueprint: SDK + auth + model-routing for CatalystPay

Thanks Monica — appreciate the concise blueprint. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we loop in ops: 

1) Auth: our preference is mTLS in prod but we need a short-term hosted OAuth path for the initial pilot. Can your hosted flow honor a restricted tenant scope where tokens are limited to inference-only and no dataset export?

2) Fallback: the proposed latency thresholds look reasonable. For the reranker path, would you recommend running the embeddings index in our cloud (we use GCP us-central1) or use Redwood-hosted indices? Cost and data residency are the drivers.

3) Structured output: we need the tool-calling sample that ensures an authorization decision is returned as a stable JSON schema (fields: decision, reason_code, confidence). Amira will validate against our downstream microservices schema.

We can schedule the technical sync — Tue 11/14 10:00am PT works for eng-ops. I’ll add our SRE (ops alias) and attach an initial security checklist.

Lee
Director, Platform Engineering | CatalystPay
lee.harper@catalystpay.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lee Harper <lee.harper@catalystpay.com>, Amira Khan <amira.khan@catalystpay.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-10T09:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo blueprint: SDK + auth + model-routing for CatalystPay

Hey team — jumping in from the infra side with a lightweight technical reply to Lee’s questions so the sync can focus on decisions: 

- Hosted OAuth scoping: yes — we support token scopes limited to inference-only. We’ll also enable request-level redaction for any fields you flag as sensitive. I’ll add the exact scope names to the Drive doc before the sync.

- Embeddings index residency: for latency and egress cost we recommend hosting the index in your GCP us-central1 project (we provide a managed connector to push vectors and run the reranker close to the index). If you prefer Redwood-hosted indices we can enable region-aware tenancy but there’s a modest monthly hosting fee.

- Structured output: attached is a sample tool-call payload (JSON) that returns the stable fields Lee mentioned. We’ll also publish a test harness so you can run 1000 synthetic calls to validate schema and latency.

- Model routing specifics: our suggested policy block for your use-case (in plain language):
  * Route read/write-sensitive authorization prompts to model-set A (high-accuracy) with concurrency cap 40 and latency SLO 350ms;
  * If queueing or tail latency > 350ms for > 2s, failover to model-set B (quantized medium) with reduced context window;
  * If model-set B is saturated, route to reranker-only path returning candidate IDs + local deterministic business logic.

Action items before Tue sync:
- Lee: confirm SRE contact and whether your legal team requires on-prem index residency.
- Monica: push the SDK starter repo to the shared Drive and include the auth snippet Ben referenced.
- Karthik/Ben: prepare a 10-slide infra brief showing mTLS cert flow and the policy JSON that can be dropped into CatalystPay's config.

I’ll bring the policy JSON. Monica — happy to join the sync.

— Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
